text:
Jamie: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel roll (attn-optim v2) we're seeing worse perceived streaming latency for short chats. p95 fine, p99 spikes during tail. anyone seen similar?
Taylor: saw this in canary. p95 steady but p99 jumps when stream chunk size is large + KV cache thrash.
Priya: can you paste the repro profile? exact microbatch, chunk, and kv settings please.
Jamie: repro run: microbatch=16, stream_chunk=64, flush_interval=120ms, kvcache=enabled (LRU 1k entries). Not huge load (~200rps).
Sam: interesting — flush_interval 120ms is aggressive for chunk=64. perceived-first-byte suffers because we wait to accumulate token chunk before flush.
Priya: quick profiler snapshot I took this morning:
```
model=redwood-7b
microbatch=16 -> p95=95ms p99=410ms throughput=520 tok/s
microbatch=8  -> p95=78ms p99=230ms throughput=320 tok/s
stream_chunk=64 -> first_byte+200ms tail spikes on p99
stream_chunk=16 -> first_byte+60ms much smoother p99
KVCache evictions correlated with p99 windows
```
Lee: kernel selection might be picking the large-seq kernel for chunk=64 which has higher cold-start overhead for short requests. switch to small-seq kernels for streaming paths?
Taylor: agree. We have a heuristic map: sequence_length_threshold=128 picks large kernel. For stream_chunk=64 combined with microbatch=16 we still trigger a path that expects long seqs.
Jamie: so options: reduce stream_chunk (16 or 8), lower flush_interval (30-50ms), or adjust kernel selection threshold. Which is lowest-risk?
Sam: lowest-risk first: reduce stream_chunk to 16 and flush_interval to 50ms for canary. That should improve perceived latency at cost of a few extra kernel calls.
Priya: also add a KV cache pinning tweak — for streaming, pin recent prefixes for 200ms beyond use so we don't evict between microbatches. small patch: kvcache.ttl_stream = 200ms.
Taylor: if we change kernel threshold we need regression tests across batch sizes. The compilation path differs and could affect throughput.
Jamie: I ran a small AB locally: chunk=64/interval=120ms (current) vs chunk=16/interval=50ms (tweak)
```
A (current): p95=95ms p99=410ms perceived_first_byte=210ms
B (tweak)   : p95=82ms p99=150ms perceived_first_byte=62ms
throughput loss ~8% at 95th percentile of sustained load
```
Lee: nice. If throughput delta is small, we can roll tune to tenant-level routing: keep chunk=64 for bulk generation routes, chunk=16 for chat routes.
DeployBot: deploy request queued: canary-stream-tune-206345 — will run against 5% of traffic. ETA 3m.
Priya: I'll push the KV TTL and stream_chunk override flags behind a feature flag so we can toggle per-route.
Sam: also adding microbatch adaptive policy: if tail p99 > target, reduce microbatch size by 2x for streaming endpoints for 30s. Should smooth tails.
Jamie: action items: 1) canary deploy chunk=16 + flush 50ms (DeployBot). 2) Priya feature flag for kvcache.ttl_stream=200ms. 3) Taylor/Lee to add kernel-threshold tests. 4) Sam to prototype microbatch autoshrink.
Taylor: logging note — add tag stream_chunk and flush_interval to token-emission traces so we can correlate in Console.
Jamie: thanks. If canary looks good, we roll to 25% and monitor p99, perceived_first_byte, and token/sec. :thumbsup:
Sam: will monitor. will post telemetry snapshot in this thread in 10m.
DeployBot: canary-started for canary-stream-tune-206345 at 2063456820
Sam: quick telemetry after 5m: canary (5%) -> p95=84ms p99=158ms perceived_first_byte=68ms throughput change -7%. Looks promising.
Jamie: perfect — let's keep it rolling and backfill tests.
Priya: i'll open a follow-up RFC with the per-route heuristics and experiments.
Lee: FYI, i'll run a kernel microbench across seq 8/16/32/64 to quantify crossover points.
Jamie: awesome team, closing the loop here once 25% is green.
